content.text: How much memory can I allocate to a Lambda function?

Lambda allows you to allocate between 128 MB and 10,240 MB (10 GB) of memory to a function in 1 MB increments. Increasing memory also proportionally increases the amount of virtual CPU allocated to your function, which can speed up CPU-intensive tasks. Next step: Use the AWS Lambda Power Tuning open-source tool to test different memory configurations and find the best balance of performance and cost for your function.

content.text: How does DynamoDB TTL work?

TTL (Time to Live) lets you define a specific attribute on your items that holds an expiration timestamp in Unix epoch format; DynamoDB automatically deletes items whose TTL attribute value is in the past, typically within 48 hours of expiration. Deletion by TTL does not consume write capacity units, making it a cost-free way to manage data lifecycle. Next step: Add a TTL attribute to your table and enable TTL in the console or via the CLI to start cleaning up stale data automatically.
